subject: general
question: Which of the following is the border between India and Pakistan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Radcliffe Line**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Radcliffe Line** is the boundary demarcation line between India and Pakistan that was established during the partition of India in 1947.
 
• It was named after its architect, **Sir Cyril Radcliffe**, who was the chairman of the Boundary Commissions for both India and Pakistan.
 
• The line was drawn based on the distribution of religious communities, primarily Hindus and Muslims, in the regions.
 
• The **Radcliffe Line** divided the British Indian provinces of Punjab and Bengal into two new countries, India and Pakistan.
 
• It has been a focal point of several conflicts and disputes between the two nations since its inception.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The partition of India led to one of the largest mass migrations in human history, with millions of people crossing the newly formed borders to join their chosen nation.
 
• The partition also led to significant communal violence, resulting in the loss of lives and displacement of populations.
 
• Several regions, including Kashmir, have remained contentious and a source of conflict between India and Pakistan.
 
• The Radcliffe Line was officially declared on **17th August 1947**, two days after India gained independence from British rule.
 
• Despite the initial chaos and disputes, the Radcliffe Line remains the international boundary between India and Pakistan to this day.
